reason: The cited evidence (E1) demonstrates a 3× TBR reduction via nanoscale trenches at a GaN/diamond interface, supporting the contact-area premise, but it concerns a different material system (semiconductor/dielectric) and does not address structural integrity, phase stability, or irradiation effects in HEAs, leaving most key premises unsupported.
premises: Nanoscale interfacial patterning reduces thermal boundary resistance (TBR) by increasing contact area.
The TBR reduction mechanism is enhanced phonon coupling across the interface.
The patterning does not introduce deleterious phases or stress concentrations that compromise structural integrity.
The intrinsic ductility and phase stability of the HEA are maintained under thermal cycling and irradiation.
A 2–3× improvement in effective thermal conductivity is achievable based on prior evidence.
